v1.2.6: "At most the VAT that 5% on households' part of the Renewables Obligation's Northern Ireland stations would have raised from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. The order (SI 2026/987) zero-rates households' electricity in Great Britain only and keeps Northern Ireland at 5% to 31 March 2027. Budget 2026 says the extended relief is expected to apply in Northern Ireland from April 2027 (paragraphs 3.4 and 6.210), so the model counts Northern Ireland at 0% from then, as it counts the extension for Great Britain. The model does not split households by area, so before April 2027 it zero-rates Northern Ireland's households too. The figure is an upper bound because Northern Ireland's households do not pay for all of these stations. Northern Ireland's stations make far more certificates than Northern Ireland's suppliers must present, and most are presented by suppliers in Great Britain, where the zero rate applies. In the year to March 2025 Northern Ireland's stations were issued 5.6 million certificates, and Northern Ireland's suppliers had to present 1.4 million."
